claim: umbrelOS 2.0.0 was published 2026-09-22; 2.0.1 (marked Latest) on 2026-11-01; 2.1.0-beta.1 (pre-release) on 2026-11-03

The OS image is built from Debian trixie in a Docker multi-stage build with the base image pinned by digest and apt pinned to snapshot.debian.org dates (image 20261027, apt 20261031, backports kernel 20261028)
amd64 and generic arm64 take kernel and firmware from trixie-backports; ZFS stays on trixie; the Raspberry Pi image takes kernel and boot firmware only from the Raspberry Pi apt repo
NVIDIA driver 595.91.07 and NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.20.1-1 are pinned in the image build; Kopia 0.23.1 and rclone 1.75.2 are pinned with per-arch SHA-256
Images are produced by Rugix Bakery with targets generic-grub-efi (amd64, arm64) and rpi-tryboot (Pi 4/5); ext4 filesystems use fixed UUIDs and hash seeds for reproducibility

Installed disk layout (x86/arm64): GPT with EFI 256M, boot-a and boot-b 512MiB, system-a and system-b 10GiB, then an ext4 data partition with 0.5% root reserve; Pi uses 128MiB boot slots and 5GiB system slots
The Pi system slot is a read-only squashfs (zstd level 19, 1M blocks); the amd64 system slot is ext4 without a journal
The image pins rugix-ctrl v1.3.2

In stable 2.0.1, umbreld asks https://api.umbrel.com/latest-release for the latest release, downloads the updateScript URL the server returns and runs it with bash -c as root; there is no signature check in this path
The 2.0.1 update script installs the Rugix bundle with --insecure-skip-bundle-verification on Rugix >= 1.0
Signed-release code (packages/umbreld/source/modules/update/, releases/, scripts/release-signing) exists at tag 2.1.0-beta.1 and does not exist at tag 2.0.1 (git ls-tree of both tags)

Trust chain: an offline root key on a hardware wallet (Bitcoin signed message) signs an approved-signers list; signers use P-256 keys created in a Mac Secure Enclave; the list sets requiredSignatures and can revoke releases by manifest hash

Devices fetch the signers list daily and before updates from api.umbrel.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, keep only the newest root-signed list, and save it durably so going back to an older release cannot forget it
Signers lists do not expire: a device that cannot reach any source keeps trusting the newest list it has seen

Install refuses a server-offered release that is not newer (semver.gt) and refuses if the manifest changed since the user's check (manifestHash binding); an explicit releaseUrl bypasses the version check

2.1 beta installs with rugix-ctrl update install --reboot set --bundle-hash <hash from signed manifest>; code comments forbid signing script-payload or incremental bundles because Rugix pipes script payloads to bash before checking the hash
The root key can be handed over to a new hardware wallet by a chain of handovers starting at the ROOT_PUBLIC_KEY built into umbreld, which never changes
umbreld commits the booted Rugix slot (rugix-ctrl system commit) as the first step of start(), before migrations, auth, apps or the web server start
commitOsPartition runs rugix-ctrl system commit and only logs an error if it fails

Rugix docs: unless an update is committed the next reboot returns to the old system; commit makes the currently booted system the default; Rugix has no built-in health check (a pre-commit hook is suggested); --reboot set may not survive a hard power cycle
No hardware watchdog configuration was found anywhere in packages/os at 6f357e18 (grep -i watchdog returned nothing); the GRUB kernel line sets panic=5
If the data partition fails to mount, Rugix keeps booting with in-memory state and umbreld enters recovery mode; if the root overlay cannot be set up it falls back to an in-memory overlay

Umbrel support page (updated 2026-10-02): updates are never installed automatically, and if an update is unsuccessful for any reason the Umbrel automatically rolls back; the page does not mention signing

claim: umbrelOS does not use Secure Boot; DKMS kernel modules are left unsigned

The app manifest (umbrel-app.yml) schema includes manifestVersion, id, port, dependencies, permissions, implements, backupIgnore, storage.dataRoot, folderAccess, environment, widgets, requiresHttps, torOnly
umbreld patches each app's Compose file before running it: it injects container_name and adds GPU device access only when the manifest lists permissions: GPU
umbrel-apps lints PRs with pull_request_target, running only trusted base-branch tooling against the PR's files treated as data

No Docker-socket or privileged-container check was found in umbreld's apps module at 6f357e18 (grep for docker.sock and privileged in modules/apps returned nothing); the ban is a store review rule, not an OS-enforced rule
Backups use Kopia; a repository can only be created on a network share or an external drive; retention is keep-latest 10, hourly 24, daily 7, weekly 4, monthly 12, annual 0

The Kopia repository password is the first 16 hex characters (64 bits) of SHA-256 of the user's backup password, and that derived value is saved in the device's settings store; the code comment calls it 128 bits; Kopia applies scrypt on top

Umbrel support (updated 2026-10-02): backups are encrypted and hourly to another Umbrel, a NAS or a USB drive; the destination needs twice the backup size; you cannot restore without the encryption password; Umbrel Private Cloud is coming soon

claim: There is one owner account that cannot be changed or deleted; members cannot install, update or configure apps, update umbrelOS, or manage backups, storage, network or users; members get their own private Home folder, Photos, 2FA and shared apps/folders
Device-management tRPC procedures are owner-only: isOwner rejects any principal whose accountId is not the owner's
Account passwords are hashed with bcrypt (bcryptjs, $2b$) and 2FA uses TOTP; a member's Samba password is stored as a plaintext secret so it can be re-applied after an OS update
MCP tokens have the form umbrelmcp_<32 hex id>_<64 hex secret>, at most 20 tokens, secrets stored hashed

MCP permissions (apps, appStore, files, manageSystem, machines, createMachines) are stored once in McpStoreSettings and shared by every token; a stored token has only label, agentType, secretHash and createdAt. Same shape at tags 2.0.0 and 2.0.1
2.0.0 release notes: 'Each agent gets its own token and only the access you allow, and you can revoke it anytime.'

Umbrel support (updated 2026-09-27): only the owner can set up MCP; agents act as the owner; MCP is in beta; the endpoint uses plain HTTP even when umbrelOS is opened over HTTPS; Hermes Agent is one of the listed agents

MCP tools are registered only if granted; the server instructions tell the agent it controls the owner account; system-management tools (OS update, restart, hostname, release channel, logs) are registered only with manageSystem

LAN ingress uses an nftables table umbrel_lan_ingress to redirect app ports to hidden Node listeners, with the app login on port 2000; automatic HTTPS uses a device-local CA (ca.pem) and server certificate
FailSafe pools are created with zpool create ... -o compatibility=openzfs-2.3 so a pool still imports after an OTA rollback to an older ZFS

Umbrel support (updated 2026-11-10): FailSafe uses ZFS RAIDZ1 on SSDs and mirrored pairs on HDDs, needs two or more internal NVMe/SATA slots, is not a replacement for backups, and Storage Manager is not available on Raspberry Pi
Machines use libvirt at qemu:///system with software TPM (swtpm) state under /var/lib/libvirt/swtpm
